quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Marisol used to dread grocery shopping because she never knew what to cook for the week. Now she plans five dinners every Sunday and buys only the ingredients she needs. She says she throws away far less food and spends noticeably less money each month.
options: Marisol Shopping Without Any Plan at All
A Habit That Increased Her Monthly Spending
Marisol Throwing Away More Food Than Before
Weekly Meal Planning Cutting Food Waste and Costs
quests.correctAnswer: Weekly Meal Planning Cutting Food Waste and Costs
quests.hint: Consider what Marisol changed about her shopping habits and the two results that followed.
quests.explanation: A new weekly planning habit leads to two clear benefits here: less waste and lower cost. Together, not separately, they explain why Marisol's new routine actually works.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: When the warehouse where Felix worked closed suddenly, he spent a nervous month searching for a new job. A former coworker eventually told him about an opening at a logistics company across town. Felix says he is grateful the warehouse closing pushed him toward a job he now enjoys far more.
options: A Sudden Job Loss Leading to a Better Opportunity
Felix Staying at the Same Warehouse Job
A Coworker Who Refused to Help Felix
Felix Disliking His New Job at the Logistics Company
quests.correctAnswer: A Sudden Job Loss Leading to a Better Opportunity
quests.hint: Notice how Felix's job situation changed and how he feels about it now, compared with when it happened.
quests.explanation: This paragraph moves from a difficult event to an unexpectedly positive outcome. The summary should capture that full arc rather than stop at the job loss.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Every other weekend, the Chens drive two hours to visit grandparents who live alone on a small farm. The grandchildren help feed the chickens while the adults catch up over coffee. Both generations say the visits give them something to look forward to between trips.
options: A Family That Visits Grandparents Once a Year
Grandchildren Who Refuse to Help on the Farm
Grandparents Who Live Next Door to the Family
Regular Farm Visits That Both Generations Look Forward To
quests.correctAnswer: Regular Farm Visits That Both Generations Look Forward To
quests.hint: Think about how often the family visits and how everyone feels about the tradition.
quests.explanation: A recurring visit that both grandparents and grandchildren look forward to is the real focus here, more than any single detail like feeding the chickens.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: When a local shoe repair shop nearly closed last year, the owner started posting short videos online showing how he fixes old shoes. The videos unexpectedly attracted thousands of viewers who had never considered repairing shoes instead of buying new ones, and business at the shop has since tripled.
options: A Shop That Closed Despite the Videos
Videos That Nobody Watched or Shared
Online Videos Reviving a Struggling Shoe Repair Shop
An Owner Who Refused to Make Videos
quests.correctAnswer: Online Videos Reviving a Struggling Shoe Repair Shop
quests.hint: Look at why the shop was struggling and what unexpected change turned it around.
quests.explanation: An unexpected marketing idea and a dramatic business recovery are directly linked in this paragraph. The summary should name both the videos and the tripled business, not just describe what the videos show.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: After her favorite restaurant closed permanently, Greta searched online for months trying to recreate its signature dish at home. She finally found a similar recipe and adjusted the spices until it tasted almost identical. Now she cooks the dish for friends whenever they ask about her old favorite spot.
options: Recreating a Closed Restaurant's Signature Dish at Home
Greta Finding the Restaurant Reopened Nearby
A Recipe That Tasted Nothing Like the Original
Greta Giving Up on the Dish After One Try
quests.correctAnswer: Recreating a Closed Restaurant's Signature Dish at Home
quests.hint: Ask yourself why Greta started searching for the recipe and what she eventually achieved.
quests.explanation: Greta's persistence pays off by the end of the paragraph, so a summary describing only her early searching, without the successful result, tells an incomplete story.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A budgeting app sends Theo a notification whenever he is close to overspending in any category for the month. At first, the alerts annoyed him, but he began checking his spending habits more carefully. Over six months, he has managed to save several hundred dollars he previously would have spent without noticing.
options: An App That Theo Deleted Immediately
Spending Alerts Helping Theo Save Money Over Time
Alerts That Made Theo Spend Even More
Theo Losing Money Despite Using the App
quests.correctAnswer: Spending Alerts Helping Theo Save Money Over Time
quests.hint: Pay attention to how Theo's relationship with the app changed and what financial result followed.
quests.explanation: This paragraph tracks a shift from annoyance to genuine savings. The summary should connect the app's alerts with the long-term benefit they produced, not just his early reaction.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Doctors at a regional clinic started offering short telehealth appointments for minor issues like colds or skin rashes. Patients who live far from the clinic say the option has saved them hours of driving each month. The clinic plans to expand telehealth hours because demand has grown so quickly.
options: Telehealth Appointments Available Only for Emergencies
A Clinic Canceling Its Telehealth Program
Telehealth Appointments Saving Rural Patients Time
Patients Who Say Telehealth Wastes More Time
quests.correctAnswer: Telehealth Appointments Saving Rural Patients Time
quests.hint: Identify who benefits most from these telehealth appointments and why demand is growing so quickly.
quests.explanation: The new appointment option matters because of a specific time-saving benefit for distant patients. A summary should connect the service to that real advantage.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A touring theater group performs short, silent comedy sketches that need no translation, allowing them to travel to towns with many different languages. Audiences of all ages laugh at the same physical jokes regardless of what language they speak at home. The group says this universal style is exactly why they chose it.
options: A Theater Group That Performs Only in One Language
A Silent Comedy Troupe Reaching Audiences Across Languages
Audiences Who Cannot Understand the Jokes at All
A Group That Travels to Only One Town
quests.correctAnswer: A Silent Comedy Troupe Reaching Audiences Across Languages
quests.hint: Focus on why the group chose silent comedy and what advantage that style gives them.
quests.explanation: Both the group's method and the reason behind it belong in the summary: silent comedy works precisely because it crosses language barriers.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: After a string of break-ins in the neighborhood, residents organized a volunteer watch group that takes turns walking the streets in the evening. Within a few months, local police reported a noticeable drop in reported incidents. Several residents say they feel safer walking home after dark now.
options: A Volunteer Watch Reducing Neighborhood Break-Ins
A Watch Group That Increased Break-Ins
Residents Who Refused to Join the Watch
Police Reporting More Incidents After the Watch Began
quests.correctAnswer: A Volunteer Watch Reducing Neighborhood Break-Ins
quests.hint: Picture why the residents organized the watch and what changed in the neighborhood because of it.
quests.explanation: The community's response led directly to a measurable drop in crime and a greater sense of safety. The summary should capture that cause-and-effect relationship, not just describe the watch group.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Diego began keeping a five-minute journal each night after his therapist suggested it might help him process stressful days. At first, he struggled to think of anything to write. Several weeks later, he says the short habit has noticeably improved how calm he feels before falling asleep.
options: A Journal Diego Gave Up After One Night
A Habit That Made Diego More Stressed
A Journal Diego Writes for One Hour Daily
A Short Nightly Journal Helping Diego Feel Calmer
quests.correctAnswer: A Short Nightly Journal Helping Diego Feel Calmer
quests.hint: Compare how Diego felt about journaling at the very start with how he feels about it several weeks later.
quests.explanation: This paragraph follows Diego from initial difficulty to a clear improvement in how calm he feels. That progression is the point, not simply a description of the nightly habit.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: This year, one high school introduced a mandatory financial literacy class covering topics like budgeting, taxes, and credit cards. Several seniors said they wished the class had existed when they were younger, since most of their friends had never been taught these basics. The school board is now considering adding the class to other grade levels.
options: A Class That Teaches Only History Topics
Seniors Who Say the Class Was Useless
A School Board Rejecting the Idea Entirely
A New Financial Literacy Class Filling a Gap for Students
quests.correctAnswer: A New Financial Literacy Class Filling a Gap for Students
quests.hint: Watch for what topic the new class covers and how students reacted to learning it.
quests.explanation: The seniors' reaction reveals a gap the class fills: financial basics many of them never learned. The summary should connect the new class with that gap rather than simply list its topics.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Construction crews widened a busy intersection near an elementary school after several parents raised safety concerns at city council meetings. New crosswalks and a longer walk signal were added as part of the project. Parents say children now cross the street with much more time to spare.
options: Parents' Concerns Leading to a Safer School Crosswalk
A City Council That Ignored Parents' Concerns
A Crosswalk That Was Shortened, Not Lengthened
Construction That Made the Intersection More Dangerous
quests.correctAnswer: Parents' Concerns Leading to a Safer School Crosswalk
quests.hint: Trace the concern from the parents' original complaint to the specific changes the city made.
quests.explanation: Citizen advocacy and concrete safety improvements are directly connected here. The summary should link the parents' concerns to the resulting changes at the intersection.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Booking a guided tour through a small local company turned out to be more rewarding than Anita expected for her trip to the coast. The guide, who had grown up in the area, pointed out hidden beaches that were not listed in any guidebook. Anita said the personal stories made the trip feel far more memorable than a typical sightseeing tour.
options: A Guide Who Only Repeated Guidebook Facts
A Local Guide Revealing Hidden Spots Beyond the Guidebooks
Anita Skipping the Guided Tour Entirely
A Tour That Avoided the Coastal Area
quests.correctAnswer: A Local Guide Revealing Hidden Spots Beyond the Guidebooks
quests.hint: Notice what made this guided tour different from a typical sightseeing trip.
quests.explanation: The guide's personal knowledge and the unlisted places it revealed are what made the experience memorable. A summary that only says a tour happened misses this entirely.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Hosting an exchange student for a semester required the Brennan family to rearrange bedrooms and adjust their usual dinner routines. At first, language differences made simple conversations slow and sometimes confusing. By the end of the semester, the family had picked up several phrases in the student's language and described the experience as one of the best things they had done together.
options: A Family That Refused to Host an Exchange Student
Conversations That Never Improved All Semester
A Family Growing Through Hosting an Exchange Student
A Student Who Left After One Week
quests.correctAnswer: A Family Growing Through Hosting an Exchange Student
quests.hint: Consider the challenges the family faced at first and how the experience had changed by the end of the semester.
quests.explanation: This paragraph traces a journey from initial difficulty to a rewarding shared experience. The summary should reflect that overall growth rather than only the early language struggles.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A small clothing shop began offering free alterations on every purchase to compete with larger online retailers that could not provide the same personal service. Customers who once shopped almost entirely online started returning to the shop specifically for the perfect fit. The owner says loyal customers now make up most of her monthly sales.
options: A Shop That Charges Extra for Alterations
Free Alterations Bringing Customers Back to a Local Shop
Customers Who Stopped Visiting the Shop Entirely
An Online Retailer Offering the Same Personal Service
quests.correctAnswer: Free Alterations Bringing Customers Back to a Local Shop
quests.hint: Think about what the shop offered that online stores could not, and how that affected its customers.
quests.explanation: A specific service advantage, free alterations, is directly tied to renewed customer loyalty. The summary should connect that offer to the boost in returning customers.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A food bank partnered with several local farms to collect vegetables that would otherwise be thrown away for being slightly misshapen. Volunteers sort and distribute the produce to families within a single day of pickup. The partnership has allowed the food bank to offer fresh vegetables for the first time in years.
options: A Farm Partnership Bringing Fresh Vegetables to a Food Bank
Farms That Refused to Donate Misshapen Vegetables
A Food Bank That Stopped Offering Produce
Vegetables That Sit Unused for Weeks
quests.correctAnswer: A Farm Partnership Bringing Fresh Vegetables to a Food Bank
quests.hint: Look at what kind of vegetables the farms provide and how quickly they reach families.
quests.explanation: The new farm partnership leads to a meaningful improvement in what the food bank can offer. The summary should connect the partnership with that fresh-produce outcome, not describe either part alone.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A small electronics repair shop noticed that many customers brought in phones with cracked screens caused by the same type of drop. The owner started offering a quick tutorial on properly applying a screen protector with every repair. Repeat cracked-screen visits from those customers dropped noticeably over the following year.
options: A Shop That Stopped Repairing Cracked Screens
A Tutorial That Increased Repeat Visits
A Repair Shop Teaching Prevention to Reduce Repeat Visits
Customers Who Refused to Learn the Tutorial
quests.correctAnswer: A Repair Shop Teaching Prevention to Reduce Repeat Visits
quests.hint: Ask yourself what extra step the shop added to each repair and what long-term effect it had.
quests.explanation: A small added service, the tutorial, leads to fewer future problems for customers. The summary should connect that teaching moment with the drop in repeat visits.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: After her doctor mentioned that her cholesterol was creeping upward, Renata gradually swapped fried foods for grilled or baked versions of the same meals. She kept the flavors she loved by experimenting with herbs and spices instead of oil. At her next checkup six months later, her cholesterol numbers had returned to a healthy range.
options: Renata Ignoring Her Doctor's Advice Completely
A Cholesterol Level That Got Worse Over Time
Renata Giving Up All of Her Favorite Flavors
Simple Cooking Swaps Improving Renata's Cholesterol Levels
quests.correctAnswer: Simple Cooking Swaps Improving Renata's Cholesterol Levels
quests.hint: Pay attention to what change Renata made to her cooking and what the result was at her next checkup.
quests.explanation: A specific dietary change and a measurable health improvement are directly linked here, and that connection, more than either fact alone, is what makes this paragraph worth summarizing well.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A small theater company decided to offer pay-what-you-can tickets for its weekday shows to attract people who normally could not afford to attend. Attendance on those nights grew far beyond what the company expected, and many new attendees later bought full-price tickets for other shows. The company now considers the program one of its most successful decisions.
options: A Flexible Ticket Program Growing a Theater's Audience
A Ticket Program That Reduced Overall Attendance
A Theater That Canceled the Program Quickly
Attendees Who Never Returned for Other Shows
quests.correctAnswer: A Flexible Ticket Program Growing a Theater's Audience
quests.hint: Identify why the theater introduced this ticket option and what happened as a result.
quests.explanation: A pricing experiment leads to unexpected long-term growth in both attendance and revenue. The summary should connect the program with that broader success, not just the ticket price itself.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A neighborhood email list started as a simple way for residents to report lost pets but slowly grew into a hub for sharing tool loans, recipe swaps, and event announcements. Members say they now know far more of their neighbors than they did before the list existed. What began as a small idea has reshaped how the street interacts.
options: An Email List That Only Discusses Lost Pets
A Pet-Finding Email List Growing into a Community Hub
Neighbors Who Know Each Other Less Than Before
A List That Residents Abandoned After a Month
quests.correctAnswer: A Pet-Finding Email List Growing into a Community Hub
quests.hint: Focus on how the purpose of the email list changed over time and what effect that had on neighbors.
quests.explanation: This paragraph traces the list's evolution from a narrow purpose to a much broader community role. The summary should reflect that overall transformation, not just the original lost-pet function.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Struggling with low visitor numbers, a museum redesigned several exhibits to let guests touch and interact with replicas instead of just reading text on a wall. Families with young children began visiting far more often than before, and the museum's director credits the hands-on approach with reversing years of declining attendance.
options: A Museum That Removed All Interactive Exhibits
Families Who Stopped Visiting After the Redesign
A Museum Director Who Opposed the New Approach
Hands-On Exhibits Reversing a Museum's Declining Attendance
quests.correctAnswer: Hands-On Exhibits Reversing a Museum's Declining Attendance
quests.hint: Picture what the museum changed about its exhibits and what happened to its attendance afterward.
quests.explanation: A specific design change is directly connected to a turnaround in visitor numbers. The summary should link the hands-on exhibits to the improved attendance trend.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A rural school district struggled for years to find substitute teachers willing to drive long distances for a single day of work. The district began offering a higher daily rate plus mileage reimbursement, and the substitute shortage eased within one semester. Several substitutes said the extra pay finally made the long drive worthwhile.
options: A District That Lowered Pay for Substitutes
A Shortage That Grew Worse After the Pay Increase
Higher Pay Easing a Rural School's Substitute Shortage
Substitutes Who Refused the Higher Rate
quests.correctAnswer: Higher Pay Easing a Rural School's Substitute Shortage
quests.hint: Notice what specific change the district made and what happened to the shortage afterward.
quests.explanation: A financial incentive is directly tied to a solved staffing problem in this paragraph. The summary should connect the pay increase with the eased shortage, not just describe the original difficulty.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: After repeated complaints about long wait times, a city's public transit agency added real-time arrival screens at major bus stops. Riders could finally see exactly how many minutes remained before the next bus, instead of guessing. Surveys later showed that perceived wait times felt shorter even though actual bus schedules had not changed.
options: Real-Time Screens Making Bus Waits Feel Shorter
Screens That Showed Incorrect Arrival Times
An Agency That Removed All Bus Schedules
Riders Who Felt Waits Became Longer
quests.correctAnswer: Real-Time Screens Making Bus Waits Feel Shorter
quests.hint: Consider what information the new screens gave riders and how that changed their experience, even without faster buses.
quests.explanation: Better information improved rider perception even though the actual schedule never changed. That distinction, not just the screens themselves, is what the summary should capture.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: When the only grocery store in a small town closed after its owner retired, residents were left without a nearby place to buy fresh food. A group of local farmers and volunteers opened a cooperative market in the empty building within a few months. Residents say the new market feels more personal than the chain store it replaced.
options: A Town That Stayed Without Any Grocery Store
Farmers Who Refused to Open a New Market
A Cooperative That Closed Within Weeks
A Community Cooperative Filling a Grocery Store Gap
quests.correctAnswer: A Community Cooperative Filling a Grocery Store Gap
quests.hint: Follow the town's grocery problem from the store's closing to the community's solution.
quests.explanation: Residents solve a sudden gap in services through collective action. The summary should connect the closure with the community's response, not just describe the loss.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A grandmother who had sewn quilts for decades began teaching free weekend classes at the community center after her grandchildren showed interest in the hobby. Word spread quickly, and now people of all ages attend, including several teenagers who had never touched a sewing machine before. She says passing on the skill has become as rewarding as making the quilts themselves.
options: A Grandmother Who Refused to Teach Anyone
Classes Attended Only by Other Grandmothers
A Grandmother's Free Classes Spreading a Quilting Tradition
A Skill That No One Wanted to Learn
quests.correctAnswer: A Grandmother's Free Classes Spreading a Quilting Tradition
quests.hint: Think about why the grandmother started teaching and who ended up attending her classes.
quests.explanation: A skill spreads across generations because of one person's willingness to teach. That ripple effect is the heart of the paragraph, well beyond her personal hobby.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A discount furniture store began offering a buy-back program where customers could trade in old furniture for store credit instead of throwing it away. The traded items are repaired and resold at a lower price, creating a more affordable option for budget shoppers. The program has also noticeably reduced the amount of furniture sent to the local landfill.
options: A Store That Stopped Accepting Old Furniture
A Buy-Back Program Cutting Furniture Waste and Costs
A Program That Increased Landfill Waste
Customers Who Refused to Use Store Credit
quests.correctAnswer: A Buy-Back Program Cutting Furniture Waste and Costs
quests.hint: Look at how the buy-back program works and the two benefits it creates.
quests.explanation: The trade-in program is tied to both lower prices for shoppers and less landfill waste. The summary should reflect that combined benefit rather than just one side of it.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A small bakery began donating unsold bread to a homeless shelter every evening instead of throwing it away. What started as a simple act of avoiding waste turned into a weekly volunteer event when shelter staff invited the bakery's employees to help serve dinner. Several employees now say it is the most meaningful part of their week.
options: A Bakery That Throws Away All Unsold Bread
A Bread Donation Growing into a Weekly Volunteer Tradition
A Shelter That Refused the Bakery's Donations
Employees Who Avoid the Volunteer Event
quests.correctAnswer: A Bread Donation Growing into a Weekly Volunteer Tradition
quests.hint: Ask yourself how the bakery's original idea changed over time into something bigger.
quests.explanation: A simple waste-reduction habit grows into a meaningful volunteer tradition here. The summary should capture that full progression rather than just the bread donation itself.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A mobile phone company introduced a simplified menu mode designed specifically for first-time smartphone users, including many older adults. Icons are larger, and unnecessary settings are hidden until a user chooses to see them. Early customer feedback shows the simplified mode has made many older users far more comfortable using their phones daily.
options: A Mode Designed Only for Advanced Users
Feedback Showing Older Users Avoid the Mode
A Company That Removed All Settings Permanently
A Simplified Phone Mode Making Tech Easier for Older Users
quests.correctAnswer: A Simplified Phone Mode Making Tech Easier for Older Users
quests.hint: Pay attention to who this new phone mode was designed for and how those users have responded.
quests.explanation: A specific design choice is tied to its intended audience's improved comfort. The summary should link the simplified mode to the positive feedback from older users.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: After noticing employees skipping lunch breaks to meet deadlines, a software company started a strict no-meeting policy during the midday hour. Productivity did not drop as managers had feared, and employees reported feeling noticeably less burned out by the end of each week. The policy has now become one of the company's most popular workplace rules.
options: A Policy That Required More Meetings at Lunch
Productivity That Dropped Sharply After the Policy
A No-Meeting Lunch Policy Reducing Employee Burnout
Employees Who Disliked the New Rule
quests.correctAnswer: A No-Meeting Lunch Policy Reducing Employee Burnout
quests.hint: Identify why the company created this policy and what effect it had on employees.
quests.explanation: A workplace rule addresses burnout without hurting productivity in this paragraph. The summary should connect the policy with both outcomes, not describe the rule alone.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Hoping to attract a few curious neighbors, a community center began hosting monthly trivia nights focused on local history. Attendance grew steadily as longtime residents enjoyed sharing memories that even surprised the event organizers. The center now keeps a growing scrapbook of local stories collected from trivia night conversations.
options: A Trivia Night Uncovering and Preserving Local History
A Trivia Night That Lost Attendance Every Month
Organizers Who Knew Every Story in Advance
A Center That Stopped Collecting Local Stories
quests.correctAnswer: A Trivia Night Uncovering and Preserving Local History
quests.hint: Notice what the trivia night was originally meant to do and what unexpected outcome it produced.
quests.explanation: A simple event grows into something that now preserves community memory. That transformation, more than the trivia format itself, is what the paragraph is really about.
